subject: Performance benchmarking / architecture deep-dive — scheduling
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finexa.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + perf benchmarking deep-dive

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the time last week. We'd love to run a technical deep-dive focused specifically on performance and latency benchmarking for the use case you described (real-time analytics enrichment). Proposed goals for the session: 
- Align on performance targets (p95 latency, concurrent requests, tokens/sec)
- Walk through architecture and where Redwood would integrate (routing, caching, batching)
- Review load-test plan and required test data
- Define success criteria for pilot

Attendees from our side: me (AEs), Rishi (account exec), Ben (Sales Engineer), Dylan (Solutions Eng). Can you confirm your team (engineer + infra)?

Proposed times (PST):
- Wed Mar 25, 10:00–11:00
- Thu Mar 26, 14:00–15:00
- Fri Mar 27, 09:00–10:00

I attached a short requirements doc and a first-pass load-test plan. If none of these windows work, share a few slots and we'll accommodate.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: finexa_requirements.pdf, redwood-loadtest-plan.xlsx

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finexa.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@finexa.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + perf benchmarking deep-dive

Hi Marissa —

Thanks — super helpful. We definitely want to do the deep-dive, but our lead infra engineer is OOO Wed–Thu and only returns Fri. Could we aim for Mon Mar 29 or Tue Mar 30 instead? Prefer mornings PT. Attendees: me, Carlos (infra), and Maya (our ML infra engineer) — I can loop her in once we lock a time.

Also quick question on goals: our primary KPI is 99th-percentile latency under production load (we're targeting <400ms for 128-token responses) and an aggregate throughput target of ~10k tokens/sec during peak ingestion. Does Redwood have benchmarking templates for validating both latency and token throughput across concurrency?

Olivia
Olivia Chen
Director of Data Products | Finexa Analytics
olivia.chen@finexa.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finexa.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + perf benchmarking deep-dive

Thanks, Olivia — that works. Monday Mar 29 morning PT is available on our side.

Quick responses to your questions: 
- We can validate both p99/p95 latency and aggregate tokens/sec. Our load-test plan includes burst/concurrency testing, steady-state throughput runs, and synthetic traces approximating your production token distribution.
- For the session we'll bring a baseline run and a proposed test harness (k6 + custom token feeder + JMeter wrappers for concurrency).
- Goal alignment suggestion: p99 < 400ms for 128-token responses; target aggregate throughput 10k tokens/sec for peak. We may also propose an initial pilot target of 5k tokens/sec to start and ramp.

Proposed slot: Mon Mar 29, 09:30–10:30 PT — we'll send a calendar invite if that works. I've attached an updated load-test plan and an annotated checklist we usually run.

If you want us to include anything specific in the test harness (sample payloads, auth flow), drop a note and we'll add it.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Carlos — we can run using temporary sandbox credentials and a short-lived test key. Action items before the session: 
- Finexa: share network constraints, sample payloads, and expected token distribution (we'll use these to seed the token feeder).
- Redwood: we'll provide test API key + a small ingress allowlist for the load generator; Ben will send the how-to and the k6 harness repo link.

Ben: can you prepare the harness and a checklist for the run? Ideally include steps for: auth, warmup, steady-state load, ramp, and teardown.

I'll send a calendar invite for Mon Mar 29 09:30–10:30 PT and attach the invite and our load-test plan.

Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@finexa.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finexa.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2026 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Calendar invite + test-harness link

All —

Invite sent for Mon Mar 29 09:30–10:30 PT (attached as benchmark-invite.ics). Repo for the harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/loadtest-harness (readme includes k6 + JMeter configs).

Quick note on test parameters I'll run during the session (and include in the spreadsheet):
- Warmup: 5 min at 1k tokens/sec
- Ramp: 10 mins to 5k tokens/sec
- Peak: 15 mins steady at 10k tokens/sec (128-token responses)
- Concurrency target: ~1k concurrent requests during peak
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU utilization, token/sec, tail latency heatmap

If we hit high error rates we can pause and adjust batching/cache config. Looking forward to it.

Ben Carter
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Attachments: redwood-loadtest-plan.xlsx, benchmark-invite.ics
